text:
[LINT.4.4] An empty interval (per [LINT.6]) overlaps no
interval, including another empty one. An empty interval has
`start == end`, so `min(i1.end, i2.end) <= i.end` and
`i.start <= max(i1.start, i2.start)` — the earlier end is at or
before the later start, and [LINT.4.1]'s strict inequality is
false.

This is a **consequence** of [LINT.4.1] and not a separate rule.
It follows directly from [LINT.7.1]: an empty interval admits no
`t`, so it shares no instant with anything, so no intersection
with it is non-empty.
